sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Zwolle, the capital of Overijssel, runs a zoned parking system in which the street gets dearer than the garages. The council adopted the Verordening Parkeerbelastingen for 2026 on 15 December 2025, in force from 19 December. In zone I, the inner city, street parking costs 4.00 euros for the first hour and 8.00 euros an hour from the second, in zone II 2.00 euros for the first two hours and 4.00 euros from the third, and in zone IV 1.50 euros an hour [5]. The first resident permit costs 225 euros a year in zone I, 70 in zone II and 50 in zone IV [5]. Paid hours in zone I run Monday to Saturday from 09:00 to 23:00 and Sunday from 13:00 to 17:00, and in zones II and IV until 20:00 [3]. Permits are capped at 80 percent of the eligible spaces in zone I, with a waiting list [4]. The framework is the Parkeerstrategie 2040, adopted on 18 December 2023, and the Nota parkeren of 31 March 2025, which splits the city into six zones, makes paid parking plus permits the standard, uses progressive street tariffs in the first three zones and sets the rule that a garage should be cheaper than the street; regulated parking is to be extended from the centre outwards in 2026 to 2030 [1][2]. A draft college decision of 16 June 2026 would extend regulated parking to five more neighbourhoods, planned for the end of the first quarter of 2027, with twelve residents' meetings drawing about 8 percent of the households written to; it was a draft and we could not check the final decision [9]. The Nota also plans tariff rises from 2028, such as 4.50 euros for the first hour in zone 1 and 3.50 euros an hour in garages, which are plans and not tariffs in force [8].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The big project is the mobility hubs. The first, Weezenlanden-Noord, an underground hub next to the provincial office, has been reduced to 426 spaces and needs an extra 7.2 million euros of credit; a council proposal of 12 November 2025 expects construction to start in mid-2027 and the hub to open in 2030, with charging at only about 2.5 percent of spaces at opening because of grid congestion [15]. During construction the college decided in principle to provide temporary parking, including about 80 places on the Goertjesweg, to be rented, and 20 extra visitor places on the Schuurmanstraat [16]. In October 2023 the college asked the council for 28.5 million euros for the Nieuwe Veemarkt hubs, one of about 225 spaces and one of about 300 along the A28, with about 950 places in the plan overall, and we did not check the outcome [17]. The Nota counts over 1,100 public charge points in Zwolle, about 50 of them in municipal car parks, and plans at least 100 more in existing garages [13].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
The municipality operates the garages Katwolderplein (700 spaces), Diezerpoort (611), Noordereiland (330 plus 340 on two levels), Lübeckplein (385), Pas de Deux (204) and Burgemeester Van Roijensingel (190), according to the national register, whose municipal live feeds were last updated in June and July 2025 [11]. The Noordereiland garage costs 3.00 euros an hour and 15.00 euros a day in 2026, and the other municipal garages 1.50 euros an hour and 7.50 euros a day [6]. Q-Park runs Centrum (323 spaces), Maagjesbolwerk (453) and the P+R at Hanzelaan, which has 207 spaces on Q-Park's own page; the register's live record gives 132, and the two were not reconciled. Its advertised starting prices are 20 euros a day at Maagjesbolwerk and 12 euros at the P+R [12]. About 2.5 million parking transactions were made in 2023, 57 percent of the street ones by phone app [14].

Our data cover the P+R at Hanzelaan, whose feed gives 132 spaces against Q-Park's 207, so the percentages are approximate. Over about 57 days since 22 August 2026 occupancy averaged about 35% on weekdays and 19% at weekends, and it reached full in a single reading on a Thursday around midday. The garages are not in our data.
